done.why: The world told me I had taken all 150 turns it allows, just as I stepped into a forest clearing I had never seen. The egg was already in the case, with the coins and the painting beside it, but the surface north and east of the house and the west ramp in the cellar were still unexplored.

about: A trimmed, re-written slice of the white house and the caverns under it. You find a jewel-encrusted egg in a tree, bring it home to a trophy case that 'expects to be filled', then go down through a trap door that bars itself behind you. Underground there is a troll, a small closed maze with a dead adventurer's bag of coins, a chasm, a looted gallery with one painting left, and a chimney that is the only way back up if you travel light. The place is about being locked below with your prizes and finding the narrow way home. Several passages are openly unfinished ('Back soon. -- The Management'), so it feels like a deliberately small, honest cut of a much larger place.

ending.what: No ending; I reached 70 of 350 points (egg, coins, painting in the case) and was stopped by the turn limit with the surface still to explore.

moments.note: Walked up the dark stairs without a lamp and got the grue warning; backed off immediately.
The trophy case has 'the patient air of something that expects to be filled' - a small line that made the goal feel like the room's own wish.
The gothic lettering translates to 'This space intentionally left blank.'
Climbed the tree and found the egg in a nest, 'scavenged by a childless songbird'.
Egg in the case: the thing I came for, done cleanly after one 'isn't open' nudge.
The trap door crashed shut and someone barred it above me the moment I went down. Nicely unsettling.
Three thrusts and the troll's head came off; the black fog eating the carcass was a good touch.
East of the Troll Room: 'The passage to the east has not been finished. A note is pinned to the rock: Back soon. -- The Management.' Charming way to admit a wall.
Maze exits are not symmetric - south took me somewhere, north would not bring me back. Took several turns to trust the markers over my instincts.
A one-way 'down' with a warning I would not be able to get back up; I did not understand the warning until I tried.
An unlisted 'up' from one maze room opened onto the skeleton, the rusty knife, the key and the bag of coins. Exploration rewarded.
The skeleton 'sat down for a moment's rest and found the moment longer than expected'.
The dead-end wall is 'solid, plain and entirely uninterested in you'.
Could not go back down the way I came up to the skeleton room; the only exit is north. Had to re-derive the map.
The skeleton key does nothing to the trap door that is 'locked from above'. Mild - I expected a key to be worth something.
The chasm: a dark 'your lamp does not so much light as annoy'. Best description in the place.
The painting 'done with such tenderness that it is hard to look at it for long, and harder to look away'.
The chimney only takes you, a light, and one more thing. Fair rule, clearly stated, but it meant a second full trip underground for the painting.
Went down the trap door again and it barred itself again. So the chimney is the only way home every time.
Stepped into a new clearing and the turn limit cut me off before I could even examine it.

wished: Explore the forest north of the tree and the clearing east of the house; the turn limit stopped me there.
Find out what the west ramp in the cellar is for, since it is described but 'unclimbable'.
Use the skeleton key on something - it opened nothing I found.
Open the egg's clasp safely; I left it alone because of the fragility warning and never learned what was inside.
Walk the unfinished east passage from the Troll Room after 'The Management' returned.
A way to know what counted as a treasure: the painting added only a few points and the coins many, and I could not tell why.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: It gave the trophy case a personality and made filling it feel like the room's request, not just a score.

lines.line: It looks extremely fragile, and extremely valuable, in that order.
lines.why: Told me exactly how to treat the egg without a rule being stated; I never touched the clasp.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: The first moment the house felt hostile; it set the tone for everything below.

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. A note is pinned to the rock: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: The world admitting its own edges with a joke rather than a blank wall; I liked it more than I expected.

lines.line: ...as though he had sat down for a moment's rest and found the moment longer than expected.
lines.why: The best sentence in the maze, and a quiet warning about the maze itself.

lines.line: The chasm drops away from your feet into a dark that your lamp does not so much light as annoy.
lines.why: A description that made me stop and reread it; the underground prose is a notch above the surface.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, a light to climb by and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A constraint stated so plainly that the second trip underground felt fair instead of punishing.

fun.why: Getting the egg home was quick and satisfying, the troll fight and the barred trap door gave the descent real tension, and the skeleton's coins behind an unlisted exit was a genuine reward for poking at every direction. The maze mapping stretch was tedious but short enough not to sour it.

engagement.why: I wanted to keep going the whole way and was annoyed, not relieved, when the turn cap hit mid-exploration. The second trip for the painting via the chimney was a plan I made and carried out, which kept me invested.

difficulty.why: The egg goal was a straight walk with one small nudge (open the case first). The troll fell in three swings. The maze is only seven rooms and markers solved it. The only real obstacles were the barred trap door and the chimney's carry limit, both of which told me plainly what they wanted.

interestingness.why: Being locked below and having to find the chimney out is a good structure, and the unfinished passages and Management note make the trimmed world feel intentional rather than broken. The maze asymmetries and one-way drops were interesting to untangle even when they confused me.

prose.why: Surface rooms are plain and functional, but the examine text underground - the chasm, the skeleton, the painting, the uninterested wall - is sharp, dry and often funny. Those lines are why I examined everything.
